review.title: Task "Normalize log levels in the sync client"

issues.title: One transport failure is logged as Error in two layers

origin.quote: Why Error here? The transport already logs this.
origin.author: reviewer
origin.verdictReason: Transport.send logs the failure at Error (src/sync_client.py:16) and SyncSession.push logs the same failure at Error again (src/sync_client.py:36).

explanation.text: One failed push writes two Error lines today: the transport logs the OSError at `src/sync_client.py:16`, then SyncSession logs it again after the last retry at `src/sync_client.py:36`. Alerting counts both.

options.label: Error once in SyncSession, transport logs Debug
Error once in the transport, SyncSession logs Debug
Keep both, add a correlation id

recommendation.reason: SyncSession is the layer that knows the push finally failed after all retries; the transport only sees one attempt.
unverified: Whether other callers of Transport.send rely on its Error line was not checked; this fixture has no other callers.

issues.title: Request logging crashes when the request has no identity

explanation.text: `src/sync_client.py:29` reads `request.identity.name`; an anonymous request has no identity, so the log call raises before the push starts.

recommendation.reason: A null guard is one line and removes a crash on every anonymous push.

issues.title: Retry attempts are logged too loud

explanation.text: Every failed attempt is logged at Warning (`src/sync_client.py:34`), so one outage writes a Warning per attempt per push before the final Error.

recommendation.reason: Only the final failure needs attention; single attempts recover on their own.

issues.title: The log says Retrying where the code gives up

explanation.text: `src/sync_client.py:37` logs "Retrying" right before the final `raise`, after the last attempt.

recommendation.reason: The Error line above already says the push failed; the extra line only misleads.
